key_provisions_or_claims: Existing Japanese standards (JIS B 8445) require consideration of children's safety but give no specific methods.
Created a mapping table of JIS and ST standards to risk assessment and risk reduction steps for child safety.
Identified gaps: active contact by children and self-moving robot collision hazards are not covered.
Recommended caregiver-directed residual risk information and hold-to-run controls against unintended child operation.
Low-speed load-cell collision experiments showed cushioning materials reduce impact force, but some increase impulse.
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper examining how Japanese safety standards (JIS B 8445, JIS Z 8050, ST toy standards) can be combined for child-safe design of personal care robots. It maps standards to risk assessment steps, identifies gaps, and reports basic low-speed collision experiments with cushioning materials.
